# codigate_identity_provider (Resource)

An identity provider that protected apps sign people in with: your own OIDC provider, or type email for one-time codes by email.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "codigate_identity_provider" "okta" {
  name          = "Okta"
  issuer        = "https://example.okta.com"
  client_id     = "0oa1b2c3d4"
  client_secret = var.okta_client_secret
  scopes        = ["groups"]
}

resource "codigate_identity_provider" "email" {
  name = "Email code"
  type = "email"
}

output "okta_redirect_uri" {
  value = codigate_identity_provider.okta.redirect_uri
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name shown on the sign-in page (at most 100 characters).

### Optional

- `client_id` (String) OIDC client id. Required for oidc.
- `client_secret` (String, Sensitive) OIDC client secret. Leave out for a public client (PKCE only). The API never returns it, so Terraform only notices a change made in Terraform.
- `groups_claim` (String) ID token claim with the user's groups. Defaults to groups for oidc.
- `issuer` (String) OIDC issuer URL (https, no query or fragment). Required for oidc.
- `scopes` (List of String) Extra scopes to request besides openid, email and profile (at most 20).
- `type` (String) oidc (default) or email. Changing it replaces the identity provider.

### Read-Only

- `has_client_secret` (Boolean) Whether a client secret is stored.
- `id` (String) Identity provider id.
- `redirect_uri` (String) Redirect URI to register at the OIDC provider (null for email).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import codigate_identity_provider.okta idp_0123456789abcdef
```
